title: Capacity and Cost Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning Record Store
Capacity Planning
Cost Model
Cloud Infrastructure
Deployment Decisions
description: A Chart.js explorer that estimates daily statements and storage from the number of active students and outlines which full-LRS deployment tier fits, comparing the single-server and distributed tiers' monthly cost ranges from the draft hardware specification.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Sizing a full LRS deployment from active students and judging the fitting cost tier
learningObjectives: The learner will judge which deployment tier fits a school or district by estimating daily statements and storage from the number of active students and comparing the result with the design's two published cost tiers.
prerequisites: The capacity model and cost model sections (Chapter 21)
Converting a per-second rate into a per-day total
The difference between a sustained rate and a burst

accessibility.notes: Each canvas has an aria-label rewritten with the current values; the message panel is an aria-live region; the fitting tier is marked with a dashed outline and named in text, not by color alone

controls.label: Duty cycle
controls.purpose: Share of peak sustained over the active window

controls.label: Show burst (5x)
controls.purpose: Report the 5x burst rate against the tier's stated burst

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Estimate, compare against published criteria, and judge
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter exploration with a live verdict and source-labeled arithmetic
keyQuestions: At what student count does the single-server tier stop fitting, and why is the move advised early?
Why does the design size by the sustained rate rather than the burst?
What costs does the monthly range leave out?
commonMisconceptions: The duty cycle changes the peak rate
assessmentOpportunities: Hand calculation of rate, statements and storage checked against the explorer
A written tier recommendation with one named risk

equations: rate = students x 0.1 statements per second
statements per day = rate x duty cycle x 36,000 s
raw GB per day = statements x 1.5 KB
assumptions: Capacity assumptions from the design's capacity model as quoted in Chapter 21
Cost ranges from the companion hardware specification, draft dated 2026-07-15 (sections 4, 5 and 8)
Tier limits: single server 1,000 stmt/s sustained (5,000 burst); distributed 10,000 (50,000 burst); move advised at 3,000-5,000
limitations: Costs are planning estimates from public cloud pricing, not quotes
Engineering time, support and one-time costs are excluded
The Neo4j license figure is a rough placeholder
